name: Maturity Model
mantra: Know where you stand, then level up deliberately.
when_to_apply: Assessing current workload capabilities across pillars
Planning incremental architecture improvements
Prioritizing investment across competing concerns
Onboarding teams to Well-Architected practices
Benchmarking progress over time
without_it: Ad-hoc improvements with no clear progression
Over-investing in one pillar while neglecting others
No shared vocabulary for current vs target state
Inability to measure architectural progress
Premature optimization before foundations are solid
key_tradeoff: Structured phasing provides clarity but risks rigidity if teams treat levels as gates rather than guidance.

name: Cost Optimization
mantra: Maximize business value per dollar spent—eliminate waste, not capability.
when_to_apply: Designing or reviewing cloud architecture budgets
Scaling workloads up or down based on demand
Choosing between service tiers or pricing models
Evaluating reliability investments against financial constraints
Adopting Infrastructure as Code for repeatable, auditable deployments
without_it: Uncontrolled cloud spend and bill shock
Over-provisioned resources sitting idle
Over-engineered solutions beyond business requirements
No visibility into where money is spent
Inability to justify cloud ROI to stakeholders
key_tradeoff: Reducing cost can compromise reliability and performance; the challenge is cutting waste without eroding the quality attributes the business requires.

name: Zero Trust
mantra: Never trust, always verify every request regardless of origin.
when_to_apply: Designing network access policies for cloud workloads
Building mission-critical systems requiring strict security posture
Implementing micro-segmentation between services
Handling requests crossing trust boundaries
Adopting defense-in-depth strategies
without_it: Lateral movement by attackers after initial breach
Over-privileged network access between workloads
Implicit trust leading to undetected insider threats
Flat network topologies exposing critical resources
Single perimeter failure compromising entire system
key_tradeoff: Stronger security verification at every layer increases complexity and may add latency versus the risk of implicit trust.

name: Four Vs Of Big Data
mantra: Assess volume, velocity, variety, and veracity before architecting any data platform.
when_to_apply: Designing a new big data platform on Azure
Evaluating whether current architecture handles data growth
Selecting storage and processing technologies
Defining data quality and ingestion requirements
without_it: Storage solutions that collapse under growing data volume
Pipelines that cannot keep up with real-time ingestion rates
Brittle schemas that break on diverse data formats
Decisions made on untrustworthy or unvalidated data
key_tradeoff: Optimizing for one V (e.g., velocity) often increases cost or complexity in another (e.g., veracity).

name: Mission-Critical Design
mantra: Treat every resource as disposable and every failure as expected.
when_to_apply: Designing systems with zero-downtime requirements
Architecting stateless application tiers
Planning for automated recovery from infrastructure failures
Deploying workloads that demand maximum reliability SLAs
without_it: Stateful dependencies create single points of failure
Manual recovery processes extend outage duration
Tightly coupled components cause cascading failures
Update rollouts introduce unplanned downtime
key_tradeoff: Maximum reliability demands higher cost and complexity from ephemeral, redundant infrastructure versus simpler persistent designs.

name: Design For Self-Healing
mantra: Let the system fix itself before anyone notices it broke.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed systems with transient failure modes
Building services that must meet high availability SLAs
Defining retry, circuit-breaker, or failover strategies
Mapping known failure modes to automated remediation actions
without_it: Transient faults cascade into full outages
Manual intervention becomes the bottleneck for recovery
Mean time to recovery (MTTR) grows unacceptably long
On-call teams burn out from preventable incidents
key_tradeoff: Automated recovery adds design and testing complexity upfront in exchange for reduced operational burden and faster recovery at runtime.

name: Drive Automation
mantra: Automate everything so humans never become your single point of failure.
when_to_apply: Designing deployment pipelines for cloud workloads
Defining testing strategies for infrastructure and application code
Establishing incident response and recovery procedures
Scaling resources in response to demand changes
Managing configuration drift across environments
without_it: Human errors during manual deployments cause outages
Inconsistent environments lead to unpredictable failures
Slow recovery times due to manual intervention steps
Undetected regressions from lack of automated testing
Configuration drift silently degrades reliability
key_tradeoff: Upfront investment in automation tooling and scripting versus the ongoing risk and cost of manual, error-prone operations.

name: Loosely Coupled Components
mantra: Decouple everything so teams can ship independently.
when_to_apply: Designing microservices or modular architectures
Multiple teams need to deploy on independent cadences
Reducing blast radius of changes
Scaling individual components independently
Migrating or replacing a single system component
without_it: One team's change breaks another team's service
Deployments require cross-team coordination and lockstep releases
Testing becomes an all-or-nothing integration nightmare
Scaling requires scaling the entire monolith
Small updates carry disproportionate risk
key_tradeoff: Independence of components increases operational complexity through more contracts, interfaces, and distributed system concerns.

name: Defense-In-Depth
mantra: Never rely on a single layer to stop an attacker.
when_to_apply: Designing security controls for a new workload
Responding to newly identified threats from threat modeling
Hardening an architecture after a security incident
Implementing Zero Trust across network, identity, and data layers
Evaluating whether a single point of compromise can cascade
without_it: A single breached control exposes the entire system
Attackers move laterally unchecked after initial compromise
Security gaps go unnoticed due to lack of overlapping coverage
Compliance audits reveal insufficient compensating controls
Over-reliance on perimeter security creates a brittle posture
key_tradeoff: Each additional security layer adds cost and operational complexity versus the risk reduction it provides.

name: CAP Theorem
mantra: Pick two: consistency, availability, or partition tolerance—you cannot have all three.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed databases or data stores
Choosing replication strategies across regions
Evaluating consistency models for microservices
Handling network partition scenarios in cloud architectures
without_it: Assuming strong consistency with zero latency cost
Designing systems that silently lose data during partitions
Unexpected unavailability when prioritizing consistency
Stale reads surprising users in eventually consistent systems
key_tradeoff: Stronger consistency increases latency and reduces availability, while higher availability risks serving stale or conflicting data.

name: PACELC Theorem
mantra: Even when things are fine, you're still trading consistency for latency.
when_to_apply: Choosing replication strategies for distributed databases
Designing multi-region data architectures
Evaluating eventual vs strong consistency models
Optimizing read latency across replicas
without_it: Unexpected latency spikes from strong consistency in distributed reads
Stale data served without understanding the trade-off
Over-engineered consistency where low latency matters more
Blind reliance on CAP theorem ignoring normal operation trade-offs
key_tradeoff: Under normal operation, lower latency requires relaxing consistency, while strong consistency demands higher latency.

name: End-To-End Automation
mantra: Automate everything from deploy to decommission—never rely on human hands for repeatability.
when_to_apply: Deploying infrastructure or application changes to any environment
Managing ongoing operational tasks like scaling, patching, or failover
Onboarding new environments or regions consistently
Reducing mean time to recovery after incidents
Enforcing compliance and configuration drift prevention
without_it: Configuration drift across environments
Slow, error-prone manual deployments
Inconsistent disaster recovery with unpredictable outcomes
Difficulty scaling operations as workloads grow
Audit and compliance gaps from undocumented manual changes
key_tradeoff: Upfront investment in automation tooling and pipeline design versus the ongoing cost and risk of manual, ad-hoc operations.

name: Blast Radius Reduction And Fault Isolation
mantra: Contain every failure before it contains you.
when_to_apply: Designing multi-region or multi-zone architectures
Deploying updates via progressive rollout strategies
Introducing new dependencies between critical components
Planning for correlated failure scenarios
Segmenting tenants or workloads in shared infrastructure
without_it: Single component failure cascades across the entire system
Regional outage takes down all customers simultaneously
Bad deployment propagates globally with no containment
Noisy-neighbor effects degrade unrelated workloads
Incident recovery time explodes due to broad impact scope
key_tradeoff: Stronger isolation increases infrastructure cost and operational complexity in exchange for limiting the scope of any single failure.

name: Design For Scale-Out
mantra: Grow wide, not tall—add units, not bigger boxes.
when_to_apply: Traffic patterns are unpredictable or bursty
Single-instance vertical limits are approaching
You need resilience through redundancy
Workload components can operate independently
Cost efficiency requires matching capacity to demand
without_it: Single points of failure under load
Costly over-provisioning of oversized instances
Hard ceiling on throughput capacity
Cascading failures during demand spikes
Inability to gracefully degrade under pressure
key_tradeoff: Horizontal scaling adds complexity in state management and coordination but removes hard capacity ceilings.

name: Observe Application Health
mantra: You can't fix what you can't see—know your healthy baseline and watch for drift.
when_to_apply: Deploying a new service or major feature to production
Defining SLAs/SLOs for a workload
Investigating intermittent or hard-to-reproduce failures
Operating distributed or microservices architectures
Preparing for scaling events or expected traffic surges
without_it: Silent failures degrade user experience undetected
Incidents discovered by customers instead of engineering teams
Root cause analysis becomes guesswork without historical health data
Cascading failures propagate before anyone notices the origin
SLA breaches go unmeasured and unaccounted for
key_tradeoff: More comprehensive observability increases operational insight but adds cost, complexity, and potential performance overhead from instrumentation.

name: Complexity Avoidance
mantra: Keep it simple or pay the price when things break.
when_to_apply: Designing new architecture components
Adding integrations between services
Reviewing operational runbooks for incident response
Choosing between custom-built vs managed solutions
Evaluating whether a new dependency is truly necessary
without_it: Cascading failures from poorly understood interdependencies
Longer mean-time-to-recovery due to opaque systems
Operational toil from managing unnecessary moving parts
Increased blast radius when a single component fails
Knowledge silos where only one person understands the design
key_tradeoff: Simplicity may limit flexibility or feature richness, but complexity multiplies every failure scenario and slows every recovery.

name: Managed Compute Services
mantra: Let the platform handle the plumbing so you can focus on performance.
when_to_apply: Scaling demands outpace your ops team capacity
Deploying containerized or microservices architectures
Reducing time spent on infrastructure patching and maintenance
Optimizing for elastic, demand-driven scaling
Greenfield projects where operational simplicity is a priority
without_it: Engineering time consumed by undifferentiated infrastructure management
Inconsistent scaling leading to performance bottlenecks
Delayed patching and increased vulnerability exposure
Over-provisioning resources due to manual capacity planning
Slower time-to-market from operational overhead
key_tradeoff: You gain operational efficiency and elastic scaling but sacrifice fine-grained control over the underlying infrastructure.

name: Quantify Operational Health
mantra: Measure everything so you never have to guess what's broken.
when_to_apply: Defining SLIs and SLOs for services
Setting up monitoring and alerting pipelines
Evaluating readiness for production deployment
Conducting incident post-mortems
Planning capacity and scaling strategies
without_it: Silent failures go undetected until customers complain
Teams rely on gut feeling instead of data for decisions
Incidents take longer to diagnose and resolve
No baseline to distinguish normal from abnormal behavior
Impossible to prove reliability improvements over time
key_tradeoff: More instrumentation increases observability but adds complexity, cost, and potential performance overhead.

name: Classify And Encrypt Data
mantra: Know your data's value, then lock it down accordingly.
when_to_apply: Storing sensitive data in cloud services
Transmitting data between services or regions
Meeting regulatory compliance requirements
Onboarding new data sources into your architecture
Reviewing existing data stores for security posture
without_it: Sensitive data exposed in plaintext breaches
Regulatory non-compliance and resulting fines
Uniform treatment of all data wastes resources on low-value data
No clear ownership or handling rules for different data types
Lateral movement attacks expose unprotected data at rest
key_tradeoff: Stronger classification and encryption increase operational complexity and latency versus the risk of data exposure.

name: Monitor The Security Of The Entire Solution
mantra: Watch everything, respond to anything—security never sleeps.
when_to_apply: Deploying a new workload to production
Designing incident response procedures
Integrating third-party services into your solution
Reviewing security posture after architectural changes
Establishing continuous compliance monitoring
without_it: Breaches go undetected for weeks or months
No coordinated incident response when attacks occur
Blind spots in logging leave attack vectors hidden
Compliance violations discovered only during audits
Lateral movement by attackers across unmonitored segments
key_tradeoff: Comprehensive monitoring increases operational cost and complexity but is essential to detect and contain threats before they escalate.

name: Predictive Action
mantra: Fix problems before they exist.
when_to_apply: Complex systems with cascading failure patterns
High-availability workloads where downtime is costly
Environments generating large volumes of operational signals
Systems with predictable degradation patterns
without_it: Reactive firefighting dominates operations
Cascading failures go undetected until impact is widespread
Operational signals are ignored until alarms fire
Repeated incidents from known patterns
Increased MTTR due to late detection
key_tradeoff: Investing in signal correlation and prediction infrastructure versus accepting reactive incident response.

name: Zero-Trust Model
mantra: Never trust, always verify — no one gets standing access.
when_to_apply: Designing access controls for critical production environments
Eliminating standing write access to sensitive resources
Implementing just-in-time privileged access workflows
Hardening environments against insider threats
Meeting compliance requirements for least-privilege access
without_it: Permanent elevated privileges become attack vectors
Compromised accounts gain unrestricted write access
No audit trail for why privileges were escalated
Insider threats go undetected due to broad standing permissions
Compliance failures around access governance
key_tradeoff: Stronger security posture at the cost of operational friction and slower access to privileged actions.

name: STRIDE
mantra: Systematically hunt threats across six attack vectors before attackers do.
when_to_apply: Performing threat modeling on a new architecture
Reviewing security of authentication and authorization flows
Assessing data integrity and non-repudiation requirements
Evaluating exposure to denial-of-service attacks
Checking for privilege escalation paths in multi-tenant systems
without_it: Blind spots in threat coverage due to ad-hoc analysis
Missed spoofing or tampering vulnerabilities
Overlooked elevation of privilege risks
No structured language for communicating threats across teams
Incomplete security reviews that miss entire threat categories
key_tradeoff: Breadth of threat coverage versus depth of analysis per vector.

name: Ten Design Principles For Azure Applications
mantra: Design every Azure application against ten non-negotiable architectural truths.
when_to_apply: Starting a new Azure application architecture
Reviewing an existing design for gaps
Onboarding teams to Azure best practices
Making key trade-off decisions during design reviews
without_it: Ad-hoc architecture with blind spots
Inconsistent design quality across teams
Reactive fixes instead of proactive design
Missed reliability, scalability, or security concerns
key_tradeoff: Comprehensive principle coverage increases design rigor but can slow initial velocity and force difficult prioritization among competing concerns.

name: Sustainable AI Design
mantra: Build intelligent systems that don't cost the earth.
when_to_apply: Designing new AI/ML workloads on Azure
Selecting model size and training infrastructure
Optimizing inference pipelines for production
Reviewing cloud resource consumption of AI systems
Setting organizational sustainability targets for technology
without_it: Unnecessarily large models waste energy and money
Carbon footprint of AI workloads grows unchecked
Over-provisioned GPU resources sit idle
No visibility into environmental impact of training runs
Sustainability goals conflict with AI adoption plans
key_tradeoff: Model performance and capability versus energy consumption and carbon footprint.

name: Least Privilege
mantra: Grant only the access needed, nothing more.
when_to_apply: Assigning roles and permissions to users or services
Configuring service accounts and managed identities
Designing control plane access policies
Reviewing existing access rights during audits
Deploying new workloads or microservices
without_it: Lateral movement by attackers through over-privileged accounts
Data exfiltration due to excessive read access
Accidental deletion or modification of critical resources
Compliance violations from uncontrolled access
Blast radius expansion when a single identity is compromised
key_tradeoff: Tighter access restrictions increase operational friction and complexity in managing permissions at scale.

name: Reduce Overhead With Managed Compute Services
mantra: Let the platform carry the burden so you can focus on what matters.
when_to_apply: Team spends significant time patching and maintaining infrastructure
Scaling requirements are unpredictable or bursty
You need to accelerate time-to-market for new features
Operational expertise for infrastructure management is limited
Cost of undifferentiated heavy lifting exceeds its value
without_it: Engineering time consumed by OS patching and runtime maintenance
Inconsistent scaling leading to outages or over-provisioning
Slower delivery velocity due to infrastructure toil
Increased attack surface from self-managed components
Higher total cost of ownership from operational overhead
key_tradeoff: You gain operational simplicity and reduced toil but sacrifice fine-grained control and may incur vendor lock-in.

name: Establish Baseline Performance And Identify Bottlenecks
mantra: You can't optimize what you haven't measured.
when_to_apply: Before starting any performance optimization effort
After deploying a new workload to production
When users report degraded experience but cause is unclear
During capacity planning exercises
Before and after architectural changes
without_it: Optimizing the wrong components while real bottlenecks persist
No way to measure whether changes improved or degraded performance
Reactive firefighting instead of proactive tuning
Wasted spend on scaling resources that aren't the constraint
Inability to set realistic SLAs or SLOs
key_tradeoff: Investing time and tooling in measurement delays immediate optimization but prevents costly misdirected effort.

name: Model Capacity
mantra: Know your limits before your users find them.
when_to_apply: Planning for expected traffic growth
Preparing for load or stress testing
Sizing infrastructure for a new workload
Evaluating whether current resources can handle peak demand
Migrating workloads to new SKUs or regions
without_it: Unexpected outages under peak load
Over-provisioned resources wasting budget
Inability to predict scaling needs
Reactive firefighting instead of proactive planning
SLA breaches due to unplanned saturation
key_tradeoff: Investing time in capacity modeling upfront versus reacting to capacity surprises in production.

name: Rehearse Recovery And Practice Failure
mantra: Practice failing so failure never catches you off guard.
when_to_apply: Before deploying critical workloads to production
After significant architecture changes
During regular game day exercises
When onboarding new team members to incident response
When recovery time objectives are not being met
without_it: Panic and confusion during real outages
Undiscovered gaps in recovery runbooks
Extended downtime due to unpracticed procedures
Stale backups that fail when needed most
Team lacks muscle memory for incident response
key_tradeoff: Investing time and risk in deliberate failure exercises versus the cost of being unprepared for inevitable real failures.
